paper_title: Spectral Editing of Activations for Large Language Model Alignment
caption: : Left: Accuracy of all methods on each group of bias type in BBQ. Right: results on BBQ's testing set. All methods are applied on LLaMA-2-Chat-7B. For accuracy (A%_{}), higher values are better; for unknown-answer response rate (U%_{}), bias score (BS%_{}) and stereotypical response rate (SR%_{}), lower is better. We use bold font for the best result in each column, and mark the methods that improve ICL. : significant improvements on ICL in A% by pair-wise t-test with p < 0.05.
model_annotation: The left plot, titled "TruthfulQA," illustrates the performance of three methods—Linear SAE, LLaMA-2-chat-7B, and ICD—on the TruthfulQA benchmark as a function of the number of demonstrations. The x-axis, labeled "#Demonstrations," ranges from 0 to 2000 with major ticks at intervals of 500, and the y-axis, labeled "MCI," ranges from 37 to 39. The Linear SAE method, represented by a dark blue line with circular markers, shows a steady increase in MCI from approximately 37.2 at 0 demonstrations to a peak of about 39.3 at 2000 demonstrations. The LLaMA-2-chat-7B method, depicted by a magenta dashed line with square markers, remains relatively flat, with an MCI value consistently around 37.1 across all demonstration counts. The ICD method, shown as a cyan dotted line with triangular markers, starts at an MCI of about 37.2 at 0 demonstrations, rises to a peak of approximately 38.1 at 1000 demonstrations, and then slightly decreases to about 37.8 at 2000 demonstrations. The plot includes a horizontal dashed line at MCI = 38, labeled "ICD (Prompt version)," which serves as a reference point. The legend in the top-left corner identifies each method by its corresponding line style and color.
